acceptance: The comment scanner identifies and decomposes command strings passed to recognized runners like ssh, watch, or xargs into individual commands for interpreter scanning
Regression test verifies comments in single-string runner invocations are detected

The whitespace check at scripts/comment_execution.py:655 still detects a nested interpreter whose path contains a space, for example `/opt/My Tools/python3 -c` under docker exec (oracle finding D4; today's develop detects it). A regression test covers it.

The cost of the broader shell gate regex is measured on the same one-commit transition run used in comment-policy-hook-saturates-shared-host (358 s wall, 276 s user CPU baseline) and reported; the change does not make that run slower.

description:
Commands passed to execution runners such as ssh, watch or xargs as a single quoted string argument were not tokenized or decomposed into subcommands. As a result, nested interpreter invocations (e.g. ssh host python -c '...') inside runner strings could bypass comment and docstring scanning. The work lives in scripts/comment_payloads.py (the RUNNER_COMMANDS table and the shell gate regex) and scripts/comment_execution.py (the Python-side runner string handling). Extend the analyzer to split runner arguments and inspect nested scripts.

PR #2821 implements this but has an oracle regression (D4, below) that must be fixed before merge.
